title: 1989 AHSME Problem 7
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle A=100^\circ,\) \(\angle B=50^\circ,\) \(\angle C=30^\circ,\) \(AH\) is an altitude, and \(BM\) is a median. Then \(\angle MHC=\)

solutions.text:
Because \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AC,\) the horizontal change from \(H\) to \(M\) is \(\frac{HC}{2},\) while the vertical change is \(\frac{AH}{2}.\) Thus \[ \begin{aligned} \tan\angle MHC &=\frac{\frac{AH}{2}}{\frac{HC}{2}}\\ &=\frac{AH}{HC}\\ &=\tan\angle ACH. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(\angle MHC=\angle C=30^\circ.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Compare the horizontal and vertical changes from \(H\) to midpoint \(M\)
Both changes are half the corresponding legs of right triangle \(AHC\)
